Sparklers for Independence Day 🇺🇸

This new red, white, and blue image shows a star cluster captured by @NASAHubble, one of our nation's most impactful scientific missions.

Called NGC 6426, this star collection is classified as a globular cluster – a roughly spherical gathering of stars held together by their mutual gravitational attraction.

Located in the outer halo of our Milky Way Galaxy, NGC 6426 is approximately 13 billion years old, making it almost as old as the universe itself.

Happy 250th, America! 🇺🇸 
 
Swipe through to see red, white, and blue reflected in our solar system, with two newly-released images of our Earth and Moon.

From Earth (blue), our home planet, we are reaching out to the Moon (white) to build humanity’s first lunar outpost. There, we’ll build an enduring human presence and prepare for our next giant leap — the first human missions to Mars (red).

#NASA #America250 #FourthOfJuly

The official FIFA World Cup ball went to space 🛰️⚽️ 

Soccer balls need to move predictably, so sports engineers carefully measure and optimize their center of mass and balance. This year, the @ISS crew recreated a 2019 experiment with the adidas 2026 Trionda to show the effect of good and bad balance in footballs. 🤩 Watching this glowing green ribbon shimmer and dance, it's easy to lose yourself completely in the magic of the moment. Turn the sound on for the full experience – the music was carefully chosen to bring you as close as possible to what I felt watching this from space 💚.

What did @NASAHubble see on your birthday?

Millions of people have visited our website to check out what our orbiting telescope was looking at on any given day — whether that's an anniversary, a holiday, or just a day that's special to them.

Now, you can check out *five* different images from the day of your choice — like the evocative Veil Nebula, which Hubble observed on July 1, 2020.

Check it out at the link in our bio!

The stars and stripes of the universe 🎆
 
New views of the cosmos from @NASAChandraXray and our other space telescopes are revealing the universe in a festive red, white, and blue. Read on to learn more about them:
 
1. This photo by Chandra and @NASAWebb shows the glowing, shredded remains of a dead star. Named Cassiopeia A, this supernova remnant sits 10,000 light-years away from Earth.
2. This nebula is named NGC 3603 and contains one of the most massive young star clusters in our Milky Way

These stars are putting on quite a show 😎⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
Nearly 18,000 light-years away, millions of sparkling stars are tightly bound together by gravity in a globe-like shape. This type of collection is called a globular cluster, and this specific one is named Omega Centauri.⁣⁣
 ⁣⁣
